deep_dive.title: The Strength of Root Cuts in an Extended Abstract Branch-and-Cut Model
deep_dive.abstract: The branch-and-cut paradigm has led to effective solvers for a wide range of mathematical optimization problems. Despite significant theoretical work on pure branching and pure cutting, less is known about their interaction. We study an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to investigate tradeoffs between branching and cutting, including the time to generate cuts. We prove that, under symmetric branching, some minimal-time tree has all cuts at the root, before the first branching node, and that there is an asymmetric setting where some minimal-time tree has no internal cuts, i.e., cuts both preceded and followed by branching. For other settings, although a root-cut tree may be suboptimal and differ substantially in structure from a minimal-time tree, it nevertheless provides a reliable approximation whose tree time does not deviate arbitrarily from the optimum. For constant cut strength and bounded time functions, we show that the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows. In addition, under a single-cut-per-path restriction, we characterize when some minimal-time tree has an internal cut. Lastly, simulations indicate that the best root-cut tree is much closer to a minimal-time tree than our worst-case approximation guarantee suggests.

deep_dive.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
deep_dive.abstract: Finding the roots of a polynomial over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ in deterministic polynomial time is a long-standing open problem. Classical deterministic methods work in the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and are efficient only when $q-1$ is smooth, which is rarely the case.   We propose a method that replaces $\mathbb F_q^\times$ by the groups of rational points of an elliptic curve $E$ and of its quadratic twist $\widetilde E$. The computation splits into an offline phase, which depends only on $\mathbb F_q$ and outputs a short \emph{elliptic preprocessing datum} $\mathcal D$, and an online phase, which processes the input polynomial. Writing $Ξ(\mathcal D)$ for the largest prime factor of $\lvert E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert\cdot\lvert\widetilde E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert$, the online phase is deterministic and finds the roots of any $f\in\mathbb F_q[X]$ of degree $n$ within $\widetilde O(Ξ(\mathcal D)^2\,n\log^2 q+n^ω\log q+n\log^3 q)$ operations in $\mathbb F_q$. A precursor of our method is an algorithm by Rónyai, which recovers the roots through Galois computations over number fields, relies on GRH, and comes with a polynomial bound of unspecified degree; in contrast, our online phase works entirely over $\mathbb F_q$ and is unconditional. Moreover, $\mathcal D$ can be certified deterministically and unconditionally in time polynomial in $\log q$ and $Ξ(\mathcal D)$.   We conjecture that every $\mathbb F_q$ of large enough characteristic admits a datum with $Ξ(\mathcal D)\leq(\log q)^{O(1)}$, and support this with a heuristic and with experiments. Constructing such a datum in polynomial time remains open.

quick_skim.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
quick_skim.abstract: For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy.   The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

quick_skim.title: Ozone groups and centers of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras
quick_skim.abstract: Let $p,q$ be roots of unity with $pq\neq1$, and put $\ell=|\langle p,q\rangle|$ and $t=\ord(pq)$. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is $μ_\ell\timesμ_{\ell/t}$, generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order $t$. We give a presentation of the center as a hypersurface over a cyclic quotient surface singularity. It is regular exactly when $1$ is a characteristic root, which disproves a conjecture of Chan, Gaddis, Won and Zhang, and Gorenstein exactly when $p^{m/h}=q^{n/h}$, where $m=\ord(p)$, $n=\ord(q)$ and $h=\gcd(m,n)$; for $p=ζ_5$, $q=ζ_5^{2}$ it is not. We also decide when the fixed ring of the ozone group is Gorenstein and when $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ is Calabi--Yau, and show that the algebras with regular center have non-affine automorphisms and nonzero locally nilpotent derivations.

quick_skim.title: DeepAVR: Deep Analysis via Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Vulnerability Repair
quick_skim.abstract: Automated Vulnerability Repair (AVR) has emerged as a critical defense against software security flaws, aiming to triage and fix bugs autonomously. Early LLM-based approaches focused on patch generation under the assumption of perfect fault localization, while recent end-to-end methods attempt to repair vulnerabilities directly from sanitizer logs. However, these methods often fail when the root cause is deeply hidden--either physically distant from the crash site or logically masked by interdependent errors--making the initial report insufficient. We propose DeepAVR, a multi-agent framework for end-to-end AVR that performs deep analysis by transforming intermediate repair outcomes into structured diagnostic feedback. DeepAVR decomposes repair into specialized roles--Fault Localization, Patch Generation, Compile Validation, Security Validation, Functionality Validation, and Patch Review--and routes feedback across these roles to iteratively refine both localization and patch hypotheses. In particular, DeepAVR introduces patch-conditioned re-localization, which treats execution results from intermediate patches as diagnostic signals to uncover hidden root causes, and a root-cause-oriented patch review stage that detects symptom-level fixes and incomplete repairs beyond execution-based validation. Evaluation on the real-world C/C++ vulnerability repair dataset VulnLoc shows that DeepAVR significantly outperforms prior methods, generating correct patches for 92.3% of vulnerabilities. Furthermore, results on SAN2VULN demonstrate strong generalization, with DeepAVR effectively repairing vulnerabilities unseen during training.

quick_skim.title: Elliptic curve rank growth in multi-quadratic extensions
quick_skim.abstract: In this article we give an algorithm to produce infinitely many explicit quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a rational point and fixed root number. Moreover, under the Parity Conjecture (or other technical hypotheses), for each $n\geq 1$, we produce explicit multi-quadratic extensions $L_n$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, of degree $2^n$, such that the growth in rank from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $L_n$ is at least $\max\{2n+2^{n-1}-1,\,2^n-1\}$ when the root number of $E$ is $-1$, and at least $\max\{2n,\,2^{n-1}\}$ when it is $+1$. As a result, assuming Parity, we exhibit elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ and extensions of degree $2^n$ where the rank after base-extension is greater than or equal to $34$ or $30+\max\{2n+2^{n-1},\,2^n\}$.

quick_skim.title: On perfectoid ideals
quick_skim.abstract: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear algebra algorithm for computing finite approximations of such generators. We illustrate this by an explicit approximation modulo $8$ of an element $σ\in (t-1)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/2^{\infty}}\rangle$ which admits compatible sequences of $2$-power roots and satisfies $σ\equiv t-1\pmod{2}$.

quick_skim.title: Asymptotic spectral properties and extreme eigenvalues of sample correlation matrices from nonstationary high-dimensional VAR processes
quick_skim.abstract: We study the limiting spectral distribution and extreme eigenvalues of the sample correlation matrix $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ from a high-dimensional vector autoregressive (VAR) processes. Depending on whether roots of the characteristic polynomial of given VAR lie on (nonstationary) or outside (super-nonstationary) the unit circle, $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ presents different types of asymptotic spectral properties. Under both nonstationary and super-nonstationary regimes, the empirical spectral distribution of $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ degenerates in probability to a point mass at zero. The rescaled extreme eigenvalues of $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ are asymptotically equivalent to the eigenvalues of a finite-dimensional symmetric random matrix determined by the characteristic roots. Moreover, under super-nonstationarity, $\hat{\boldsymbol{R}}$ degenerates in probability to a matrix with finite rank.

quick_skim.title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
quick_skim.abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant security risk for large-language-model (LLM) applications and agents, yet the field still lacks a coherent map of how these attacks are constructed. More than twenty public datasets describe prompt injection using incompatible vocabularies, often organized around delivery vector, attacker goal, or generation method. In this Systematization of Knowledge, we present PIAtlas, a taxonomy organized instead around how the injected instruction is constructed to subvert the underlying model. Its six classes, one per subversion mechanism, form the roots of a hierarchy of techniques and sub-techniques that researchers can use to describe attacks consistently and design more systematic evaluations. We derive the taxonomy from how LLMs are trained, prompted, and influenced by human-like framing, and compare it with historical attack data. To ground this comparison, we release PICorpus, to our knowledge the largest license-clean collection of public prompt-injection datasets, and map thousands of its records to PIAtlas under a human-verified protocol. The mapping shows that attacks usually combine several techniques drawn from only a few mechanisms. It also reveals gaps that existing labels obscure: widely used agent benchmarks test only part of the attack space, and adaptive attackers favor mechanisms that curated benchmarks underrepresent. PIAtlas thus provides a common foundation for understanding this attack space, improving benchmark coverage, and guiding red teaming and defenses.

quick_skim.title: A $u$-$p_w$ SPH framework with mechanical-hydraulic boundary treatment in GeoDualSPHysics for large-deformation geomechanics
quick_skim.abstract: Pore-water pressure changes the effective stress and deformation of saturated geomaterials, while skeleton deformation generates pressure and drives drainage. Resolving this feedback together with hydraulic boundary conditions is necessary for simulations that connect consolidation to large post-failure movement. This paper presents a hydromechanical extension of GeoDualSPHysics using a single-layer displacement-pore-water-pressure ($u$-$p_w$) smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) framework. An explicit pressure-rate equation combines volumetric compression and Darcy diffusion, and the resulting pore pressure feeds back into the skeleton momentum balance. The implementation extends the existing modified dynamic boundary condition (mDBC) infrastructure to carry hydraulic ghost values alongside mechanical boundary data. Prescribed pressure at drained surfaces is combined with impermeable walls and impermeable loaded contacts, with separate control of loading and drainage activation. The formulation is assessed through one-dimensional consolidation, two-dimensional flexible-strip loading, and the three-dimensional Cryer problem. The Cryer simulations reproduce the non-monotonic central pressure response over four Poisson ratios, with normalized pressure root-mean-square errors of 0.012-0.030. The consolidation tests also expose remaining settlement and late-time pressure discrepancies. Applications to 5 m and 8 m sensitive-clay slopes illustrate sequential retrogressive failure and large deformation. The contribution is the integration of hydraulic feedback and boundary handling within GeoDualSPHysics; the results establish an initial verification basis while identifying remaining accuracy and convergence questions.

quick_skim.title: Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups
quick_skim.abstract: Let $G_d$ be the subgroup of index $d>1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and put $G_d^0=G_d\cup\{0\}$. For a covering $A+G_d^0=\mathbb{F}_q$ with $\#A=s$, we prove $q\le d^{8s/d}$ by shifting the roots of a Bonferroni polynomial. Although a uniform bound in $s$ alone must allow exponential growth, our estimate confines such growth to bounded indices and gives polynomial bounds when $s/d$ is bounded. A cubic specialization gives bounds of degree at most eight for $s\le2d$. For shift sets of logarithmic size, higher moment estimates give a uniform covering-probability formula, including the critical window. Together with the index restriction, this determines the covering indices of almost every shift set of size $\lceil k\log q\rceil$ for each fixed integer $k\ge2$.   A subfield construction attains the order of the uniform restriction on the index. We determine its covering number exactly and prove minimality under subgroup inclusion. We also characterize equality in the elementary counting bound by subfield cosets. Fixing a subfield as the shift set in a quadratic extension leads to a sharper projection bound, attained by an infinite family with unique representations outside the shift subfield.

quick_skim.title: Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
quick_skim.abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $α<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in regressions involving general nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We demonstrate that the proposed methods---including IVX-based and related instrumental-variable procedures---facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes nearly and mildly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/α<d<2-1/α$, where $α\in(1,2]$. Our analysis is applicable to both parametric and kernel regression models. The finite-sample performance of the proposed methods is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study. Additionally, we provide an empirical application to the predictability of stock returns using long-memory heavy-tailed predictors.

quick_skim.title: Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $Q_{p,q}(t)$ via the Rank-One Chabauty-Coleman Method
quick_skim.abstract: Let $Q_{p,q}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$10$ second cuboid polynomial, with coprime positive integers $p\ne q$. We prove that $Q_{p,q}(t)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and hence over $\mathbb{Z}$. More generally, the normalized associated quintic $P_s(x)$ and its composition $P_s(t^2)$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $s\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0,\pm1\}$. The proof reduces linear and quadratic factors to rational points and horizontal conjugate pairs on one fixed genus-$2$ curve. A certified rank upper bound for its Jacobian, together with an exact divisor calculation, gives a rank-one annihilating differential at the prime $3$. For the quadratic-factor case, the symmetric coordinates of a horizontal pair lie on an explicit double cover of an elliptic quartic. All rational affine points on this model are $3$-adically integral and reduce to six smooth residue classes. The pulled-back differential is a unit in each class, proving that six displayed points form the complete list. Their coordinates exclude every admissible parameter. A negative real root of the irreducible quintic then supplies the additional degree argument required for irreducibility of the degree-$10$ polynomial. The rank computation and all exact arithmetic certificates are specified explicitly for reproduction.
